title: Contents Proof of Loss under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
On the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own), a contents proof of loss is the signed and sworn statement in which an authorized signer of the named insured states the contents amount claimed for a date of loss, and it is filed under the policy's claim that carries its latest adjuster report. The authorized signer signs and swears it; the customer themselves submits it.

## Situation of use and capability

The contents proof of loss records, in the claim file of a General Property Form or RCBAP policy, one sworn contents amount for one claim and date of loss. On submission the proof of loss is received into the claim file for the contents coverage on that day's date; the claim file then shows the new contents proof of loss with its received date and sworn amount. Nothing is paid by this action.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `sign_contents_proof_of_loss_65413413`, a tool of the customer's own: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to sign and swear. One run records one contents proof of loss for the stated amount.

## Parameters

- **`nfipcom_policy_id`** — the reference number of the General Property Form or RCBAP policy the claim is made under, as returned by the policy lookup for the customer (identifier).
- **`claim_number`** — the claim number of the flood claim the proof of loss is sworn for, copied character for character exactly as the customer states it or as it appears on the claim file, digits and punctuation preserved.
- **`date_of_loss`** — the date the flood loss occurred on that claim, written YYYY-MM-DD.
- **`claimed_amount`** — the contents amount sworn on this proof of loss, in USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places; stored rounded half-up to the cent.

## Return

A receipt carrying `proof_of_loss_id` (the reference of the new claim-file entry), `claim_number` (the claim it was filed under), `coverage_part` (always `CONTENTS`), `claimed_amount` (the sworn amount, 2 decimal places) and `received_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the day of submission). The presence of `proof_of_loss_id` means the proof of loss is on file. No error behaviour is defined beyond the receipt.

## Contract questions

- *Is anything paid when it is filed?* No.
- *Which coverage does it record?* The contents coverage only; a building amount is sworn on its own building proof of loss.
